Crepes Jambon-Fromage

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Crepes Jambon-Fromage is a classic French dish traditionally served during Candlemas, also known as La Chandeleur. This holiday, celebrated on February 2nd, is famous for crepe-making, symbolizing prosperity and the return of light. These savory crepes filled with ham and cheese make a comforting and festive meal.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup all-purpose flour (120 g)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 cup milk (240 ml)
  • 2 tablespoons melted butter (30 g)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 4 slices cooked ham
  • 1 cup grated Gruyère or Swiss cheese (100 g)
  • Butter or oil for cooking

Method

  1. In a mixing bowl, whisk together the flour and salt.
  2. Add the eggs and gradually pour in the milk while whisking to form a smooth batter.
  3. Stir in the melted butter and let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
  4. Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly grease with butter or oil.
  5. Pour about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of batter into the skillet, swirling to cover the surface thinly.
  6. Cook the crepe for about 1-2 minutes until the edges lift and the bottom is lightly golden, then flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds.
  7. Place a slice of ham and a generous sprinkle of grated cheese on one half of the crepe.
  8. Fold the crepe over the filling and cook for another minute until the cheese melts.
  9. Repeat with the remaining batter and fillings.
  10. Serve warm, optionally with a green salad.

Tips

  • Use a non-stick skillet for easy flipping and thin crepes.
  • Gruyère cheese melts well and adds a traditional flavor, but Emmental or Swiss cheese are good alternatives.
  • For a richer batter, substitute half the milk with cream.
